fileDoc.description: Provides a core allocator specification and concrete implementations inspired by Zig's std.mem.Allocator design: - Arena: bump allocator for fast, bulk-freed temporary allocations - Pool: fixed-size object pool for uniform allocations - StackAllocator: LIFO allocator for short-lived scratch data All allocators implement the Allocator spec and work with the `alloc T(args) in allocator` syntax.

doc.summary: The core allocator specification.
doc.description: Any type implementing Allocator can be used with the `in` keyword to direct allocations to a specific backing store: var arena = Arena(1024) var p = alloc Point(1.0, 2.0) in arena

doc.summary: A bump/arena allocator that allocates linearly from a fixed-size region.
doc.description: Allocations are extremely fast (pointer bump). Individual frees are not supported; instead, all memory is released at once via `reset()` or when the arena is destroyed. This is the primary tool for avoiding leaks with short-lived data. Everything allocated in an arena shares a common lifetime. Ideal for: - Frame-scoped temporary data in game loops - Scratch buffers for parsing or rendering - Any pattern where allocations share a common lifetime Usage: var arena = Arena(64 * 1024) var particles = alloc Real[1000] in arena var transforms = alloc Real[1000] in arena // ... compute ... arena.reset()   // all allocations freed at once Or with region blocks: region(32 * 1024) { alloc -> var verts = alloc Real[600] in alloc } // everything freed here

doc.summary: A fixed-size object pool allocator.
doc.description: Pre-allocates a fixed number of equally-sized slots. Allocation and deallocation are O(1). When a slot is freed, it is returned to the pool for reuse. Ideal for: - Entity/component systems with bounded object counts - Network connection pools - Particle systems with a fixed maximum - Any pattern requiring many same-sized allocations Usage: var pool = Pool(slotSize: 32, slotCount: 1000) fin slot1 = try pool.acquire() fin slot2 = try pool.acquire() pool.release(slot1)     // slot1 returned to pool fin slot3 = try pool.acquire()  // reuses slot1's memory

doc.summary: A LIFO (last-in, first-out) stack allocator.
doc.description: Allocations and deallocations follow strict LIFO order. Freeing must happen in the reverse order of allocation. This is ideal for function-scoped scratch data where allocation lifetimes are nested. Compared to Arena: - Arena: no individual free, bulk reset only - StackAllocator: individual free in LIFO order, plus bulk reset Usage: var stack = StackAllocator(4096) fin a = try stack.alloc(64) fin b = try stack.alloc(128) stack.free(128)  // frees b stack.free(64)   // frees a
